title: No Boatman Washed Rama's Feet
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2(44-46) (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.50-52)

captions.instagram:
Did a boatman really wash Rama's feet before taking him across the Ganga?

Many of us know the boatman Kevat who washed Rama's feet before taking him across the Ganga. Valmiki's Ramayana tells it differently: Guha is a king and Rama's dearest friend, the one who washes Rama's feet that night is Lakshmana, and at dawn Rama simply boards a boat and the boatmen row them across. The Kevat story comes from Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas.

Which version did you grow up with: Kevat washing Rama's feet, or Lakshmana? Tell us where you heard it 👇

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2(44-46) (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.50-52)

captions.youtube_description:
Did a boatman really wash Rama's feet before taking him across the Ganga?

Many of us know the boatman Kevat who washed Rama's feet before taking him across the Ganga. Valmiki's Ramayana tells it differently: Guha is a king and Rama's dearest friend, the one who washes Rama's feet that night is Lakshmana, and at dawn Rama simply boards a boat and the boatmen row them across. The Kevat story comes from Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas.

Which version did you grow up with: Kevat washing Rama's feet, or Lakshmana? Tell us where you heard it 👇

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2(44-46) (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.50-52)
Verses:
• Guha, king of the Nishadas, Rama's friend dear as his own self, lived at the Ganga — 2.44.9
• Guha embraced Rama: 'This place is yours just as Ayodhya; what may I do for you?' — 2.44.12
• That night Rama and Sita lay on the ground; Lakshmana washed Rama's feet — 2.44.25
• Guha, bow in hand, stayed awake with Lakshmana guarding Rama — 2.44.26
• At dawn Rama saw a boat at the bank, boarded with Sita and Lakshmana; boatmen rowed them across — 2.46.61-66
• Mid-river Sita joined her palms and prayed to the Ganga — 2.46.67-68
• No boatman washes Rama's feet and there is no bargaining at the boat in the CE crossing (2.46) — 2.46 (chapter)
• Kevat washing Rama's feet before the crossing is from Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas (Ayodhya Kand) — secondary

verify_note: CE 2.44–2.46 read: Guha is king and Rama's friend (2.44.9-12); Lakshmana washes Rama's feet that night (2.44.25); Guha keeps watch (2.44.26); at dawn Rama sees a boat, boards, boatmen row across (2.46.61-66); Sita prays to Ganga mid-stream (2.46.67-71). Kevat's foot-washing at the boat: Tulsidas, Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand.
